> 天对地，日对月，明对暗，阴对阳，雨对风。

The last chapter is a manual. Not a farewell, not a summary of doctrine — a manual for answering questions.

*After I pass, each of you will be a teacher in one region. I will now teach you how to speak so that you do not lose the root.*

Then the kit: three categories, thirty-six pairs, and one instruction repeated three times — 出没即离两边, come out and enter, immediately leave both sides.

## 三科: the classification as a field guide

Five aggregates: form, feeling, perception, formation, consciousness. Twelve entrances: six dusts outside, six gates inside. Eighteen realms: six dusts, six gates, six consciousnesses.

Then the sentence that turns a list into a system: *the self-nature can contain all dharmas — this is called the storehouse consciousness. If it gives rise to measurement, that is the turning consciousness. It produces the six consciousnesses, emerges through the six gates, sees the six dusts — thus the eighteen realms all arise as functions of the self-nature.*

The classification is not a map of the universe. It is a description of how a world appears through a body, with a single source named at the top. Every item in the three categories is downstream of one thing, which is why the pairs that follow can be used as a teaching device rather than as trivia.

## 出语尽双

The instruction of method:

*When someone asks you about dharma, your words should come out in pairs, all taking the paired dharma. Coming and going as mutual conditions, in the end both dharmas are removed, and there is no further place to go.*

*If someone asks about the existent, use the nonexistent as the pair; asked about the nonexistent, use the existent. Asked about the ordinary, use the sage; asked about the sage, use the ordinary. The two paths condition each other and produce the meaning of the middle way.*

Worked example: *What is darkness? Answer: brightness is the cause, darkness is the condition; when brightness is gone, darkness is — using brightness to manifest darkness, coming and going as mutual conditions, the middle way is established.*

This is a technique for breaking a question's premise without contradicting the questioner. It does not supply a third answer; it shows that the two answers on offer were each dependent on the other, and that the dependence was the thing being asked about.

## Thirty-six pairs, thirty-three of them

Here the received text does something that the commentary records and does not smooth over.

The chapter announces 三十六对 — thirty-six pairs — and then lists thirty-three. Count them: heaven-earth, sun-moon, bright-dark, yin-yang, rain-wind; good-evil, right-wrong, birth-extinction, permanent-impermanent, joy-suffering; giving-stinginess, advance-retreat, white-black, out-in, old-young; great-small, long-short, high-low, noble-base, moving-still; delusion-wisdom, foolish-smart, disorder-concentration, precepts-non, straight-crooked; real-empty, with-mind-without-mind, form-emptiness, mark-nature, conditioned-unconditioned; affliction-bodhi, birth-death-nirvana, good-root-evil-root.

Seven groups. Five, five, five, five, five, five, three. Thirty-three.

The later Zongbao edition fills the number to thirty-six by reorganizing the pairs into three classes: five for the insentient external world, twelve for dharmas and language, nineteen for the self-nature's arising function. The book's appendix prints the Dunhuang list as it stands, counts it as thirty-three, notes the three-pair gap, and does not patch the text — 照录不补.

What to do with a canon that miscounts its own list. The answer this edition takes is to keep both facts: the name as transmitted, and the list as transmitted. The number is a teaching device, and a device that has drifted is evidence about how the text was carried — assembled, annotated, renumbered — not a defect to be quietly corrected. A reader who is told thirty-six and shown thirty-three learns something a reader who is shown a tidied thirty-six cannot: that this book has a history, and that the history is visible.

## 真假动静偈

The verse he leaves on the difference between stillness and death:

*All is without reality; do not take what is seen as real. If you take it as real, that seeing is entirely unreal. If you can have your own reality, leaving the false the mind is real. If the mind does not leave the false, where is the real? Sentient beings understand movement; the insentient do not move. If you cultivate the practice of immobility, you are the same as the insentient. If you seek true immobility, there is immobility upon movement. Immobility that is mere immobility has no buddha-seed. Able to distinguish marks, the first principle is unmoved.*

The distinction is between an immobility that is the absence of motion and an immobility that is present in motion. The first belongs to stones; a stone has no buddha-seed because nothing can happen in it. The second is the one being recommended: distinguish everything, and the first principle does not move.

## 末后一偈

His last verse is four lines that read like a withdrawal:

*Still and silent, not cultivating good; free and easy, not creating evil. Quiet and hushed, cutting off seeing and hearing; vast and open, the mind without attachment.*

*Not cultivating good* is not permission to harm. It removes the project of self-improvement as a possession — the good that is done in order to be the kind of person who does good. *Vast and open, the mind without attachment* is the same word as the third principle in chapter four, 无住, at the end of the book.

Then he sits until the third watch, says *I am going*, and dies. The disciples weep; he had told them not to. Two of them had understood, and one of them, Shenhui, does not weep — which the text records not as coldness but as the only correct response to someone who has just spent a chapter explaining that the dharma has no coming or going.

## The test

Pick one pair from the list that you live inside — say, busy and idle. Answer as if asked: which are you? Then answer with the other side. Then notice what appears in the gap between the two answers. That third thing is not an answer, and it is what the pairs were for.
